transcript:
This message comes from University at Buffalo,
where scientists are working to protect the Great Lakes
and freshwater supplies around the world
from harmful contamination.
Learn more about their research at buffalo.edu/npr.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
We're learning more about the people who confronted a gunman
during an elementary school shooting in Bend, Oregon, Thursday.
The shooting killed three children and a teacher.
Oregon Public Broadcasting's Bryce Dole has the story.
The gunman was a 16-year-old former student.
Police say he jumped a fence with a shotgun
and a backpack full of ammo.
He shot at a person in a pickup truck
after the driver confronted him,
then blasted his way through the school's locked doors.
The gunman then opened fire in a special education classroom.
Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz described what happened next.
A teacher in the classroom threw her cell phone at the suspect
and then tackled him and fought to take the firearm from him.
She was not injured in that incident,
but she almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed.
A parent who had seen the shooting outside the school
followed the gunman inside
and shot him multiple times with a handgun, killing him.
Two other people were shot --
a 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher.
They're receiving care at regional hospitals.
For NPR News, I'm Bryce Dole.
The No Kings Coalition, known for its large protests
against President Trump, is taking another issue today --
voting. As NPR's Ava Berger reports,
thousands of events are scheduled for today.
Superhero capes and masks.
That's what you'll find at Cammie Dunford's
"Voting Is Your Superpower" event today in Frisco, Texas.
I have a T-shirt that says "Voting Is My Superpower,"
and I have the cape, and, uh, yeah, we're ready.
Dunford and her advocacy group, Indivisible Frisco,
also made 500 mini goodie bags.
In each one are QR codes with resources on voting in Texas.
Dunford's event is one of thousands across the country.
They're all part of the No Kings Vote Early initiative.
Unlike past protests, organizers say the goal today
is direct, nonpartisan action --
getting people out to the polls.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
Fire crews continue to battle a wildfire in Southern California
that is threatening hundreds of homes in San Juan Capistrano.
Steve Futterman reports.
The battle to contain the fire is taking place
on the ground and from the air,
with helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft
dropping water and fire retardant on hot spots.
The biggest problem for firefighters
are powerful Santa Ana winds,
which are pushing flames in different directions.
Naomi Jones' home was not damaged,
but she was still shaken.
To see the whole neighborhood, it's heartbreaking.
Orange County Fire Captain Steve Consialdi says
it could take some time before the danger is over.
We'll be here for a number of days protecting all the homes.
The winds are expected to continue during the weekend,
but they should be less intense.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman
in San Juan Capistrano, California.
At least six homes have been burned so far.
You're listening to NPR News.
Indian police have detained the founder
of the popular youth group, Cockroach Janta Party.
The group, which started as an online satire
and attracted millions of followers,
has been campaigning for the resignation
of India's top election official.
And Piers Omar Kandikar has the story.
India's opposition parties and pressure groups
like Cockroach Janta Party have demanded
that the election chief, Kyanesh Kumar, step down.
They accuse him of manipulation
in favour of the ruling BJP party
after the election commission
deleted more than 130 million names
from India's voter rolls.
Hundreds gathered in Central Delhi,
defying police orders, restricting protests.
They chanted slogans against the election commissioner
and the prime minister,
even as the security forces in riot gear
tried to break up the crowd.
The Cockroach Janta Party said
police detained their founder
before he could join the demonstration.
Omkar Kandikar, NPR News, New Delhi.
Pope Leo is expected to leave the hospital today
following surgery for lung cancer.
The Vatican says the Pope will lead prayers
in St. Peter's Square tomorrow.
It will be his first public appearance
since he underwent surgery just days ago.
Meanwhile, the Vatican reports, for the first time ever,
the number of Catholics in Africa has surpassed Europe.
Africa's Catholic population now stands at 288 million.
That's slightly ahead of Europe's 287 million.
The Americas, though, are still the region
with the largest number of Catholic residents.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Bend, Oregon elementary school shooting by 16-year-old former student kills three children and a teacher
No Kings Coalition holds nonpartisan voting events nationwide, including Cammie Dunford's event in Frisco, Texas
Wildfire in San Juan Capistrano, California threatens hundreds of homes as Santa Ana winds push flames
Indian police detain founder of Cockroach Janta Party amid protests demanding election chief's resignation
Pope Leo expected to leave hospital after lung cancer surgery and lead prayers in St. Peter's Square
Vatican reports Africa's Catholic population surpasses Europe's for the first time
